evidence.why: Weights, channel setup, 159-iteration count and suspicious pre-delay pointer store.
Two all-pass stages precede damping, then the third all-pass and wet/dry integer output; final sample is emitted separately.

facts.rationale: Corrects the ordering of damping relative to the third all-pass stage and makes the actual output scale explicit without concealing the exceptional pre-delay implementation.
facts.value: Processes one 160-sample channel in place through three parallel comb delays, two serial all-pass stages, a persistent damping recurrence, and a third all-pass stage. It has an optional pre-delay branch and mixes the final wet signal with the original input using weights 0.6*level and 0.6*(1-level), respectively, before truncating to integer samples. The pre-delay pointer-update sequence is suspicious in the canonical source and is not established as a correctly functioning circular buffer.

evidence.why: Main-loop signal flow, recurrence, integer conversion and pre-delay store.
Persistent comb/all-pass and low-pass state writeback.

facts.rationale: Replaces the inaccurate all-pass/damping ordering and unconditional claim that pre-delay position is correctly written back into AXFX_REVHI_WORK.
facts.value: Converts signed integer input to floating point and optionally reads/replaces a pre-delay sample. Three comb feedback paths consume this signal and their delayed outputs are summed. The sum passes through AP[0] and AP[1], then forms history = 0.3*AP[1]_output + damping*previous_history; AP[2] consumes this history. The final result is 0.6*level*wet + 0.6*(1-level)*original_input and is stored using fctiwz. Comb/all-pass offsets and last outputs, plus the damping history, are saved to the selected work-state bank. The pre-delay branch instead stores its advanced pointer at preDelayPtr(r30), where r30 holds the delay-line base, so correct work-state pointer persistence must not be assumed.

evidence.why: Pre-delay endpoint calculation, selected work base and actual store base.
Repeated pre-delay sequence and final channel-state persistence.

facts.rationale: Preserves supported channel continuity while explicitly distinguishing the anomalous pre-delay state update from normal delay-line wrapping.
facts.value: Selects an independent channel bank and advances comb/all-pass byte offsets by four per sample, resetting them to zero on equality with their recorded lengths. Final offsets, delay last outputs and lpLastout[channel] are saved for the next block. For nonzero preDelayTime, the source compares the advanced pre-delay pointer with base + 4*(preDelayTime-1), then stores it through preDelayPtr(r30), with r30 holding the line base rather than the selected work-bank base r28. Both main and final-sample paths contain this sequence; ordinary circular pre-delay persistence is therefore uncertain.
